style.vernacular: Very wet coastal capital: low and mid-rise concrete-block and plastered buildings, often unpainted grey or faded pastel with rain streaking and rust stains, under corrugated zinc roofs; old Americo-Liberian houses and churches recall the American South with porches and gables, while 1960s Capitol Hill government buildings are plain modernist blocks. Streets are asphalt on main roads, laterite and mud elsewhere, with palms, mango and rubber-type broadleaf trees and hand-painted signboards everywhere.
style.ornament: Americo-Liberian verandahs, gables and simple classical columns on older houses and churches; hand-painted advertising boards and murals on shopfronts; plain exposed concrete balconies and sun-breaks on 1960s-70s public buildings.

sources.what: early Americo-Liberian architecture reminiscent of the southern United States; tropical monsoon climate with about 4,600 mm rain a year; Capitol Hill government buildings
1960s Capitol Hill buildings designed in a modern style by Tommaso Valle
